extracted.intended_audience: NBA fans, sports writers, and readers interested in league rules and operations
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and summarizing notable rules and standards from the NBA's operations manual (2014-15) for a general sports audience. Focused on operational requirements, conduct rules, facility standards, and procedural limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chewing gum during the National Anthem
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s illegal for a player to chew gum during the National Anthem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of trades for dressed players
rubrics_metrics.description: No player dressed for a game can be traded until after it’s completed, including NBA Development League appearances. Teams may agree to a trade during the game but it cannot be executed while the game is in progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver claim fee
rubrics_metrics.description: It costs a team $1,000 to make a waiver claim, payable to the NBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mascot / in-game entertainer conduct regarding dummy likenesses
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s illegal for any mascots or in-game entertainers to abuse 'dummy likenesses' of referees or opposing players/coaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits mocking/abusive use of referee/opponent likenesses by in-arena performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft and noisemaker restrictions in arena
rubrics_metrics.description: Blimps may not land on or fly over the court. No foghorns, vuvuzelas or didgeridoos are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety and fan-experience restrictions banning certain aircraft activity and high-decibel/noise devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated negotiators and media comment limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams are required to assign no more than two 'designated negotiators' to represent the franchise in communication with free agents and their representatives. Until one of the two acknowledges interest in a free agent to the media, no one else in the organization — coach or public relations director — can comment publicly on the targeted player.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties for breaking the rules may climb as high as $1 million each; typically one negotiator is the general manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeout and intermission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A regular timeout is a minute and 40 seconds, although the rules specify the ball is put back in play at a minute and 50 seconds. The 20-second timeout is similarly extended to 30 seconds. Halftime is 15 minutes while quarter breaks are two each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exact durations for timeouts and breaks and the clock/play resumption timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arena environmental conditions (temperature and humidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required temperature for games is 65–72 degrees Fahrenheit; maximum humidity for an NBA game is 55 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to maintain acceptable conditions can affect play (example: LeBron James cramp game due to broken air conditioner and sweltering temperature).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court material, readiness, and maintenance schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts must be made of maple of 'second and/or better' grade. Courts must be replaced every 10 years (extension can be requested upon inspection by the league). The floor must be ready at least four hours before the game, 'vacuumed and then mopped.' They also need to be sanded at least every fourth season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies material quality, replacement interval, pre-game readiness procedures, and routine maintenance frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Player days off policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Each NBA player is entitled to 16 days off each regular season (October through mid-April). Those days are calculated per individual player (tracked when one is traded or claimed off waivers). A day off means no games, practice, promotional events or travel, and an NBA Development League assignment does not provide a loophole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some days off occur during the All-Star Break, although not for participants; days off are individually tracked and enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-arena music restrictions and approved prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: The home team in-arena music cannot play a song like 'Three Blind Mice' to criticize an official. Songs that can be played while the visiting team is on offense include 'Addams Family,' 'We Will Rock You,' 'Day-O,' 'If You’re Happy and You Know It,' 'Jaws,' 'Mexican Hat Dance,' and a small list of other generic prompts, like the 'defense' chant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies prohibitions on music used to disparage officials and lists permitted songs/tones for game situations.
